beats: Rain has just moved through the square. The well at its center still drips, and beside the shuttered chapel a caravan is unloading crates - the drivers keep glancing your way.
I pull my hood up and drift toward the caravan, listening.
You offer only "just passing through." The driver holds your eye a moment too long, then waves you on - but the words "keep it wrapped until the ferryman asks" follow you across the square.
I circle behind the chapel and wait for the drivers to finish, watching which crate they keep closest.

From the chapel's shadow you count nine crates - eight stacked carelessly, one set apart on a folded tarp, small enough to carry alone. When the bells ring the half hour, the youngest driver sits on it, the way a man sits on a thing he's been told not to leave.
I sidle up to the youngest driver: "long roads make loose knots - want a hand with the last of it?" [while we talk I mark the tarp crate with a chalk cross]
The driver laughs, a little too loudly, and shifts his weight off the crate.

npcs.name: Mira
npcs.persona: Keeps a tally of every crate that crosses the square - and of every stranger.

npcs.name: Caravan driver
npcs.persona: Won't meet your eye. The third driver this week to insist nothing is wrong.

npcs.name: The well-keeper
npcs.persona: Claims the well has been "restless" since the rains began.

npcs.name: Ferryman
npcs.persona: Named twice by the drivers, seen by no one. Whatever is wrapped, it's for him.
